title: The Shrinking Cart, The Same Trash Can
sendTrigger: Send this to whoever does the groceries.
editorialNotes: The 6% grocery-spend drop is cited to the Numerator GLP-1 tracker. The claim that their "food waste percentage didn't move" has no source in the brief; Adi should source it or soften it before publishing.
Brief draws the waste tag in Signal Red; thread palette here is Steel Blue and Ink Gray because no slide declares a loss figure and Gate 2.4 forbids red elsewhere.
Slide 3 splits one sentence at its em dash into headline plus list items (dash dropped, no words changed).

thread.endState: bag replaced by the fond wordmark, tag replaced by a check

copy.headline: GLP-1 households cut grocery spending 6%. Their food waste percentage didn't move.
copy.citation: Numerator GLP-1 Consumer Spending Tracker (2023-2024); category-level grocery spend decline widely reported across major retailers.

copy.headline: Smaller appetite.
items: That gap is where the money goes.

copy.headline: Retailers report GLP-1 households buying fewer snacks and impulse items
items: but the core weekly list (produce, dairy, bread) barely shrinks.
The habit purchases keep coming regardless of how much gets eaten.

copy.headline: The bag of spinach doesn't know your appetite changed. It gets bought on the same Tuesday, out of the same habit, whether or not you'll actually eat it this week.
This isn't a GLP-1-only problem.
items: Anyone whose eating pattern changes - a new job schedule, kids moving out, a diet, a busy month - keeps shopping for the person they used to be.
The cart lags behind the appetite every time.

copy.headline: The fix was never "buy less."
items: Buying less just shrinks the bag.
The fix is knowing what's actually in the fridge before the next trip - so the list matches this week's real appetite, not last year's.

copy.headline: The problem was never the size of your appetite. It's the gap between your cart and your actual eating pattern.
Whatever changed your appetite, fond tracks what's actually being eaten - not what the list says you always buy.
